cases.description: Passing a null algorithm string should trigger an IllegalArgumentException because the method validates the argument at the very beginning.
The method treats the literal "HMAC-MD5" as an alias for the RFC name and returns the constant HMAC_MD5.
The same alias works when the supplied string already ends with a trailing dot.

group: Exact RFC name match (with and without trailing dot)

cases.description: Exact match against a Name key that includes the trailing dot should return the corresponding Name constant.
Exact match against a Name key without the trailing dot should also succeed because the method checks both forms.
The lookup is case‑insensitive, so a mixed‑case string should still resolve to the proper Name.

group: Fallback to Java algorithm name (value map)

cases.description: When the supplied string does not match any Name key, the method searches the map values (Java algorithm names). "HmacSHA384" should map to the HMAC_SHA384 Name.
If the string cannot be resolved by either the key set or the value set, the method must throw an IllegalArgumentException indicating the algorithm is unknown.
Lower‑case alias for MD5 should be recognised and return the constant HMAC_MD5.
Mixed‑case alias with a trailing dot should also resolve to the HMAC_MD5 constant.
An empty string is not null, so the method proceeds to lookup and ultimately throws an IllegalArgumentException because no algorithm matches.
Leading/trailing whitespace is not trimmed; the lookup fails and an exception is thrown.

group: Trailing dot with Java algorithm name

cases.description: Java algorithm names are stored without a trailing dot; adding a dot makes the lookup fail.
Exact RFC name without trailing dot, lower‑case, should map to HMAC_SHA224.
Exact RFC name with trailing dot and upper‑case letters should map to HMAC_SHA224.
Mixed‑case RFC name that includes a trailing dot must resolve to the HMAC_SHA512 constant.
A leading dot is not part of any defined algorithm name, so the method should reject it.
Java algorithm names are stored as "HmacSHA256"; a lower‑case version should still match because the lookup is case‑insensitive.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException with message "Unknown algorithm: hmac sha256"
cases.description: The algorithm string contains an internal space, which is not part of any defined name; lookup fails and an IllegalArgumentException is thrown.
Two trailing dots do not match any RFC name nor any Java algorithm name, causing the method to throw an IllegalArgumentException.

group: Leading dot with Java algorithm name

cases.description: A leading dot is not part of any Java algorithm name; the lookup fails and the method throws an IllegalArgumentException.
The supplied string matches the prefix of a known algorithm but has an extra suffix, so it is not found and results in an IllegalArgumentException.
A newline character at the end of the algorithm string prevents a match; the method throws an IllegalArgumentException.
A trailing tab character is not trimmed, causing the lookup to fail and an IllegalArgumentException to be thrown.
A string consisting of only a dot does not correspond to any algorithm name, resulting in an IllegalArgumentException.
